languages.intro: {n} languages, each with an overview, official docs and lessons.
languages.noLessons: Lessons for this language have not been written yet. New lessons will be added through content packs.
lesson.verification.authored: Written from official sources; not yet independently reviewed
lesson.partialTranslation: This lesson is {pct}% translated into {lang}. Missing parts are shown in Azerbaijani or English.
lesson.clickLines: Click any line to see its explanation.
quiz.intro: You need at least {pass}% to complete the lesson. Just opening it does not count.
quiz.failed: The passing score is {pass}%. Read the explanations and try again.
exercise.solutionAfterHints: The solution unlocks after you have seen every hint (Settings → Learning).
exercise.selfCheck: Code in this language cannot run inside the app yet. Run it in your own editor and compare it with the solution yourself.
fields.intro: {n} development fields with their languages, technologies and roadmaps.
fields.roadmapMissing: The roadmap for this field has not been written yet.
fields.contentNote: Lessons, exercises, projects and career resources will be added in later content packs.
frameworks.intro: {n} frameworks, libraries and tools with links to official documentation.
frameworks.contentNote: Installation, configuration, core concepts and code examples will be added in later content packs.
progress.intro: A lesson counts as completed only when you score at least {pass}% on its knowledge check.
progress.avgNote: Based on your best result in each attempted lesson.
progress.weakNone: No weak topics. Results below the passing score appear here.
progress.resetConfirm: Delete all lesson progress on this device? This cannot be undone.
search.intro: Search languages, lessons, keywords, errors, technologies and comparisons. Search runs on your device; nothing is sent to the internet.
search.placeholder: Search: async, for, variable, an error message…
search.shortcut: Shortcut: Ctrl+K from any page. You can also type without special letters (ə → e, ş → s).
search.noFavorites: Add results to favourites with the ☆ next to them.
search.none: Nothing found. Try another word or the English term.
explain.intro: Paste code to see what each line does and what every keyword means. The analysis uses local rules — no AI is involved.
explain.privacy: Your code never leaves this device.
explain.chooseLanguage: The language could not be detected — choose it from the list.
explain.defined.variable: `{name}` is a variable created in this code on line {line}.
explain.defined.function: `{name}` is a function defined in this code on line {line}.
explain.defined.parameter: `{name}` is a parameter of the function on line {line}.
explain.defined.loopVar: `{name}` is the loop variable from line {line}; it takes a new item on each step.
explain.defined.class: `{name}` is a class defined in this code on line {line}.
explain.wordUnknown: This word is not in the knowledge base and is not defined in this code. It may come from elsewhere or from a library.
explain.limits: Limits: local rules recognise the most common constructs (one statement per line). Multi-line expressions and complex syntax are shown as "not recognised" rather than guessed. Execution-flow tracing and output prediction are not available yet.
errors.intro: Paste an error message from your IDE, compiler or terminal. For recognised errors you get the meaning, likely causes and fixes.
errors.placeholder: For example: NameError: name 'total' is not defined
errors.noMatch: The library has no pattern for this message. We say so rather than give an unreliable explanation.
errors.tip1: Paste the last line of the message (the error type and text) in full.
errors.tip2: If the message is localised, try the English version — the patterns match English texts.
errors.causesNote: These are the most common causes of this error; your code was not inspected, so the actual cause may differ.
compare.intro: Compare the same concept side by side in two languages: syntax, typing, memory management, strengths and limitations.
compare.snippetNote: Only the relevant lines are shown; in Java, C#, C++ and Go the code must sit inside a class/function (`main`) with the needed imports.
compare.profileNote: Performance depends on the specific task and implementation; general statements are approximate.
settings.privacy.saveSearchHistoryHint: The last 50 searches are kept on this device only.
lab.intro: Write code and run it right away. JavaScript and SQL run in a safe, isolated environment.
lab.noOutput: The code ran but printed nothing.
lab.timeoutHelp: The code hit the time limit and was stopped. The usual cause is a loop that never ends or an uncleared `setInterval`.
lab.checkPassed: Correct! The output matches the expected output.
lab.checkFailed: Not yet — the output differs from what is expected.
lab.rt.sql: SQL — built-in SQLite (WebAssembly), loaded on first run
lab.rt.python: Python — needs an additional runtime (not available yet)
lab.rt.other: Other languages — editing and explanation only, no execution
lab.safetyText: Every run happens in a separate, freshly created worker with no access to the app's data, files or the network; there is a 3-second time limit (6 for SQL) and an output size limit. SQL always runs on a fresh in-memory practice database — your real data is never touched.
practice.intro: Reinforce what you learned by writing code. Every task runs your code and checks it automatically.
practice.modeHelp.challenges: Progressively harder tasks (●○○ → ●●●). A task counts as solved when your code produces the right output.
practice.modeHelp.debug: Each task contains code with a deliberate bug. Find it and fix it.
practice.modeHelp.predict: Read the code and predict what it prints before running it.
practice.modeHelp.practice: Each lesson's practice exercise. JavaScript and SQL exercises are checked automatically inside the lesson.
practice.hintAfterTry: Hints unlock after your first attempt — try it yourself first.
practice.solutionLocked: The solution unlocks after at least two attempts and all hints (Settings → Learning).
practice.practiceText: Lesson exercises live inside each lesson. In JavaScript and SQL lessons you can write and check your code right there.
practice.buildMode: Build mode (building small projects) will be added together with the Project Center.
exercise.passed: The exercise passed the automatic check.
settings.general.learningModeHint: Decides which mode Interactive Learning opens in.
notes.intro: Your own explanations, code examples and study notes. Everything is saved automatically on this device.
notes.empty: No notes yet. Start with "New note".
notes.pick: Pick a note on the left or create a new one.
notes.bodyPlaceholder: Write in Markdown: # heading, - list, `code`, ```python code block```
notes.markdownHelp: Markdown: # heading, **bold**, *italic*, - list, - [ ] task, > quote, `code`, ``` code block (highlighted with a language name), [link](https://…).
library.intro: Keep useful code snippets with explanations, search them and reuse them.
library.sort.title: By title
library.pick: Pick a snippet on the left or create a new one.
library.explanationPlaceholder: What does this code do and when is it used? (Markdown)
flashcards.intro: Remember terms with spaced repetition (SM-2): hard cards come back often, easy ones rarely.
flashcards.emptyHelp: No cards yet. Add a starter deck below or create your own card.
flashcards.starterHelp: Creates cards from the knowledge-base keywords. Their text follows your lesson language.
flashcards.nothingDue: No cards are due right now.
roadmap.intro: A step-by-step path towards your goal. Lesson steps complete automatically when you pass their knowledge check.
roadmap.reviseHelp: Your result in these lessons is below the passing score.
roadmap.assessHelp: Two short questions pick a path for your level and goal. You can change it any time.
roadmap.goalQuestion: What do you want to become?
roadmap.autoStep: Completes automatically when you pass the lesson's knowledge check
roadmap.addStepPh: Your own step, e.g. "Finish a small project"
roadmap.goalPh: E.g. "Get my first job in 3 months"
projects.intro: Manage your projects, tasks and notes in one place, and learn by building with guided projects.
projects.empty: No projects yet. Create one or start one of the guides below.
projects.guidesHelp: Each guide has objectives, milestones, testing tips and a starter file. "Start this project" copies the milestones into your project as tasks.
projects.localNote: Project data is stored on this device. Opening a project folder from disk and reading its Git information is not available yet — you can add the repository link.
projects.name: Project name
projects.noLinkedNotes: No notes are linked to this project.
projects.newNote: Write a note for this project
projects.deleteBody: The project, its tasks and notes will be deleted. Linked notes in My Notes are kept. This cannot be undone.
cheatsheets.title: Cheat sheets
cheatsheets.intro: Concise syntax references for {n} languages and tools. Works offline.
cheatsheets.searchPlaceholder: Search code or explanations, e.g. loop, JOIN, flex…
cheatsheets.resultsCapped: Showing the first {shown} of {n} results. Refine your search.
cheatsheets.noBookmarks: No bookmarked sections in this sheet yet. Press ☆ next to a section title.
cheatsheets.fallbackNote: Some explanations are not translated into this language yet; they are shown in Azerbaijani or English.
cheatsheets.offlineNote: Snippets are shortened. See the official documentation linked in each sheet for details.
git.title: Git & GitHub
git.intro: {n} topics on Git, GitHub and the developer ecosystem: explanations, commands, common mistakes, practice and knowledge checks.
git.groupDesc.git: Version control: commits, branches, merging, working with remotes and team workflows.
git.groupDesc.github: GitHub for hosting projects, collaborating, automating and publishing.
git.groupDesc.platforms: Other code, package and knowledge platforms developers use every day.
git.section.what: What it is and why it matters
git.exerciseNote: Do the exercise in your own terminal or browser; the app does not run any commands for you.
git.tryViz: Try it in the Git Visualizer
git.vizNote: See how commits and branches change on an interactive graph.
gitviz.title: Git Visualizer
gitviz.intro: Type Git commands in a safe sandbox and watch the commit graph change live.
gitviz.safe: Everything is simulated: no real repository, file or server is touched.
gitviz.freeIntro: Try any command on a cloned sandbox repository. You can simulate a teammate pushing with `sim teammate`.
gitviz.serverEmpty: The server has no commits yet.
gitviz.notInitialized: No repository — start with `git init` or `git clone`.
gitviz.logEmpty: Type a command, e.g. `git status`. Type `help` for the full list.
gitviz.inputHint: Enter runs, ↑/↓ browse previous commands, `clear` empties the terminal.
gitviz.explainEmpty: A short explanation appears here after each command.
gitviz.notYet: Goal not reached yet — type the steps in the terminal.
visual.intro: Hard programming concepts as simple step-by-step diagrams: memory, recursion, HTTP, the event loop and more.
visual.notFound: This topic does not exist. Choose one from the list below.
visual.keys: Tip: you can also move between steps with the ← and → keys.
security.title: Cybersecurity & Kali Linux Academy
security.intro: {n} topics: security fundamentals, Linux, networking, defensive security, web security, an introduction to Kali Linux and safe lab exercises.
security.safety: This section is educational and defensive. It contains no attack instructions, exploit code or material for use against real systems. Vulnerabilities are explained only from the point of view of prevention.
security.integration: Kali Linux / WSL integration is not available in this app. The app never executes commands: examples are for reading only. To practise, set up an isolated virtual machine on your own computer (kali.org/docs).
security.legal: For authorised and legal use only. Apply what you learn here only to systems you own, in an isolated lab on your own computer, or with the owner's written permission. Unauthorised scanning or access can be a criminal offence.
security.readOnly: For reading only — the app does not run these commands.
security.roadmapHint: Not sure where to start? Open the "Learning roadmap" topic.
